Definition: Ramoth-Gilad, a place East of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Ramoth-Gilead is a place east of the Jordan, a city of refuge and a bone of contention between Israel and Syria. Ahab said, 'Know ye that Ramoth in Gilead is ours, and we be still, and take it not out of the hand of the king of Syria?'; the prophets said, 'Go up'; and Joram went up with Ahaziah to war against Hazael there.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that Ramoth-Gilead is where flattery killed a king: four hundred prophets said go up, and Micaiah alone said the LORD had put a lying spirit in their mouths — and Ahab went up and died.
